title: Acute Stroke Recognition: FAST, Mimics and Time-Critical Assessment
subject: Emergency Triage
preview: FAST highlights Face weakness, Arm weakness and Speech disturbance; Time means activating emergency assessment without delay.
quickRevision: FAST highlights Face weakness, Arm weakness and Speech disturbance; Time means activating emergency assessment without delay.
A posterior-circulation stroke can present with gait ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria or severe imbalance even without classic FAST findings.
Record last-known-well time and assess urgent brain imaging to separate ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: FAST highlights Face weakness, Arm weakness and Speech disturbance; Time means activating emergency assessment without delay.
Check capillary glucose because hypoglycemia can mimic stroke and may be rapidly reversible.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: A posterior-circulation stroke can present with gait ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria or severe imbalance even without classic FAST findings.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech disturbance, Time to activate stroke care.
FAST does not reliably cover all posterior circulation presentations: new ataxia, diplopia or severe imbalance still require urgent evaluation.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A normal initial noncontrast CT does not rule out early ischemic stroke.
